Learn more > College basketball heavyweight are set to meet under the lights on Sunday night.Few sides have garnered as many headlines over the years as UConn and UCLA. Both sides captivate the masses, albeit for different reasons. The Huskies have been a buzzsaw in recent campaigns, capturing gold twice in the past three seasons. They fell short of the mountaintop in 2025. But they've returned with a vengeance in 2026, emerging as one of the nation's best sides during the regular season. Dan Hurley's side fell short of a Big East title, suffering a 20-point defeat to St. John's in the last game of the conference tournament. But a solid display against Furman should boost morale ahead of its tilt with the Bruins.Mick Cronin's bunch might have its warts. But it performed admirably in Big Ten play, scoring wins over Purdue, Illinois, Nebraska and Michigan State during the regular season. UCLA wasn't at its best during its first-round matchup with UCF. But few teams were. Ultimately, the tournament is about surviving and advancing. The Bruins did that against the Golden Knights. Who is to say that can't keep the good times rolling against UConn, too?With that, here's what you need to know about the broadcast information for Sunday's game between UCLA and UConn.What time is UConn vs. UCLA today?Date: Sunday, March 22Time: 9:10 p.m. ETThe Huskies and Bruins will tip at 9:10 p.m. ET on Sunday night, about 25 minutes later than originally scheduled. It's the penultimate game of Sunday's slate, followed only by Texas Tech and Alabama's 9:45 p.m. ET tilt.While set to take place at 8:45 p.m. ET, the start time for Sunday's game is subject to change depending on how long it takes for Kansas vs. St. John's to conclude. Both games are set to be competed at the Viejas Center in San Diego, with the Jayhawks and Red Raiders' joust slated to start at 5:15 p.m. ET.What channel is UConn vs. UCLA on today?TV channel: TNTLive stream: DIRECTVTNT will have the broadcast of UConn and UCLA's second-round tilt on Sunday. Andrew Catalon will serve as the game's play-by-play analyst, while Steve Lappas will offer analysis in the booth.
